statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity futures completed their weekly settlement at 21:00Z, so the entire published 24-hour window covers a halted market in which no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold and no danger window is published, because the forecast horizon contains no U.S. cash session and no CME futures session. Existing-position management and emergency protection rules are unaffected by this assessment. The first genuine repricing checkpoint is the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls outside this window.
headline: Hawkish Warsh repricing closes a softer Nasdaq-100 week; futures halted for the weekend
body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks on Friday reset September policy expectations, with market-implied odds of a rate increase rising to roughly 60% from about 35% a day earlier. The repricing was expressed mainly in rates and metals: the 10-year yield closed at 4.72% (+5bp) near its session high, the 2-year traded up around 11bp to about 4.34%, and gold futures fell 3.43% to $4,504.10. Equity damage was contained and internally split. Cash NDX closed at 29,433.43 (-0.70%) and NQ futures settled the week at 29,509.50 (-0.63%), both in the lower part of their session ranges, but the decline was rotational rather than broad: semiconductors were uniformly weak (NVDA -4.6%, ARM -5.9%, INTC -2.7%) while Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet all closed higher. VIX eased to 14.43, showing no equity volatility stress. Crude was quiet, with WTI at $83.39 (-0.11%) and Brent at $88.31 (-0.26%), and the Iran sanctions track is being read as an economic rather than a physical-supply confrontation. The decisive structural fact for this window is that CME equity futures are now halted until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which sits beyond the 24-hour horizon. With no venue open, a persistent no-retracement price path cannot form, so Tail is published at a low floor throughout and Stress steps down from the closing-hour reading. Confidence stays high because Friday's closing levels, yields, oil, volatility and the seven-day calendar are all verified; it decays only gradually across Saturday as the last live observation ages.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours ran quiet until Friday's Jackson Hole speech. Overnight Asian and European hours held Tail near 11-13 with Stress in the high 40s to low 50s and a mixed mode. Tail and Stress lifted through the U.S. morning as Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish remarks reset September rate expectations, peaking at Tail 22 and Stress 64 in the 17:00Z hour with an event/whipsaw mode as yields rose and gold fell sharply. Price discovery stayed orderly: retracements occurred, VIX eased rather than spiked, and the index decline was rotational, led by semiconductors against firmer megacap software. Scores fell back to Tail 12 and Stress 52 by the 20:00Z hour as the cash session closed. One slot, the 10:00Z hour, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published window runs from the 21:00Z weekly CME settlement through Saturday 20:00Z and therefore contains no cash or futures session at all. With no venue open, the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form, so Tail is held at a 6-8 floor and Stress decays from 30 to a low-20s baseline overnight before drifting back up modestly late Saturday as the interval to the Sunday reopen shortens. Confidence starts at 86 and eases to 82 as the last live observation ages. Weekend Jackson Hole follow-up coverage and the unresolved roughly 60% September hike probability are treated as conditional inputs to the Sunday 22:00Z reopen gap, not as drivers inside this window. No calendar item prints before Monday's Dallas Fed index, and the next-week macro slate runs from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday to payrolls on Friday.
